## What was actually run

Nothing on this site was hand-written from memory. The Go reference tab is rendered
from a **godoc snapshot taken from the pinned clone of the target repository**:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin.git          # at 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646
sourcey godoc -m . -p ./... -o godoc.json                # Sourcey v3.6.12, Go 1.26.0
sourcey build                                            # renders the site from sourcey.config.ts
```

## Why an ecosystem audience would link this

`gin` is one of the most used Go HTTP frameworks: its public surface (`gin.Engine`,
`gin.RouterGroup`, `gin.Context`, the `binding` and `render` packages) is what
application code calls, and it is the part of the codebase that changes most often.
A godoc-style reference for a **specific commit** is what a maintainer needs when a
released version and `main` disagree, and what a downstream team needs when a
dependency is pinned in a lockfile and the upstream docs have already moved on.
This site answers that question for one pinned commit, from the source of that
commit, with nothing hand-maintained in between.
